capabilities: Encrypt and decrypt notes with a GPG key pair from the note context menu
Encrypt all notes automatically upon modification
Choose between OpenPGP.js and a GnuPG CLI wrapper as backend
Use OpenPGP smartcards such as YubiKey or Nitrokey through the local GnuPG installation
Configure password memory duration and how the file recovery core plugin handles encrypted notes
extras: README warns that encrypted notes may still be stored unencrypted on disk due to Obsidian caching or coredumps. Mobile is supported only with the OpenPGP.js backend. Limitations: Markdown files only, no signature support, no symmetric encryption. Includes FAQ, manual install steps, and dev/test commands.
intentEvidence: meld-cp partly inspired me with his Meld Encrypt plugin.
problem: Obsidian stores notes as plain text files on disk, so sensitive notes are readable by anyone with access to the vault folder.

relations.evidence: meld-cp partly inspired me with his Meld Encrypt plugin.
It integrates OpenPGP.js or your local GnuPG installation.

summary: Encrypts Markdown notes with GPG via OpenPGP.js or a local GnuPG installation, including OpenPGP smartcard support.
